sections.h2: Where do you record a deed for a house in Warren County?
sections.html:
At the Warren County Clerk's Office, inside the Warren County Courthouse at 413 Second Street in Belvidere. The office takes every document that affects ownership or transfer of residential, commercial and industrial property in the county, and it accepts them in person, by mail or electronically.

  • Main office: 908-475-6211.
  • Records room: 908-475-6011.
  • Public records inquiries: 908-475-6220.
  • Fax: 908-475-6208.

Hours are 8:00 am to 4:30 pm on weekdays, and the clerk's contact page asks visitors to call ahead and book an appointment so staff can serve each person efficiently. A seller whose closing is set for a late afternoon should have the title company confirm the recording method in advance.

sections.h2: What kind of county is Warren County for a seller?
sections.html:
A large, mostly rural county on the Pennsylvania line. Warren County sits in northwestern New Jersey along the Delaware River, across from Easton, Pennsylvania, and it was carved out of Sussex County in 1824. Belvidere is the county seat. Phillipsburg is the most populous of its 22 municipalities, with 15,249 residents in 2020, while Hardwick Township has the most land area and the fewest people.

The county covers 356.54 square miles of land, and the Census Bureau's 2025 estimate of 112,953 residents works out to roughly 300 people per square mile in 2020 terms. Hackettstown has the county's only NJ Transit rail stop, and long commutes are common: the mean trip to work is 34.0 minutes, longer than in many New Jersey counties.

Housing here leans toward owners. About 75% of homes are lived in by their owners, which means most deeds recorded in Belvidere come from household sales and not from landlords.

sections.h2: What does the Warren County Clerk charge to record a deed?
sections.html:
A deed costs $40 for the first page and $10 for each additional page, plus a $10 tax abstract that applies to some documents such as deeds, court orders and easements. The charges below come from the clerk's posted State of New Jersey fee schedule.

Selected Warren County Clerk recording charges, from the clerk's posted fee schedule
ItemCharge
Deed, first page$40
Deed, each additional page$10
Mortgage, first page$30
Mortgage assignment, discharge, release or postponement, first page$40
Cancellation of mortgage$20
Data recording page, paper documents$10 (or $20 if missing)
Each name after the first five$6
Inheritance tax waiver$15
Certified copy$5
Copy of any document$2 per page

The schedule adds that the county charges nothing toward the homeless fund, and that a veteran's DD-214 filing is free of charge.

sections.h2: What is the Data Recording Page, and who needs it?
sections.html:
It is a cover sheet the clerk uses to index the land record, and paper recordings without it carry a $20 indexing charge instead of $10. The clerk's recording services page says all land recordings filed on paper, and electronically recorded deeds, must include it.

For documents sent through e-file, the page is required for deeds only. Your title company or attorney normally prepares it with the deed, but if you are handling a family transfer yourself, download the form from the clerk's website and attach it to the first sheet. A missing page is an avoidable $10 surcharge and a possible delay.

sections.h2: What state fee applies when a Warren County deed is recorded?
sections.html:
The New Jersey Realty Transfer Fee, which is collected on top of the clerk's recording charges. The state sets it by the consideration stated in the deed, and the Division of Taxation's own FAQ gives two worked amounts: $1,910 for a $325,000 deed with no exemption, and $475 for a $280,000 deed where the seller qualifies for the senior citizen partial exemption.

  • An Affidavit of Consideration (RTF-1) must be filed with any deed that claims a full or partial exemption.
  • The state lists 16 reasons for a full exemption, and partial exemptions exist for seniors, blind or disabled owners, low and moderate income housing and new construction.
  • A deed recorded in the wrong county must be re-recorded in the county where the land sits, with a refund application to the State on Form RTF-3.

For Warren County sellers the last point matters because Phillipsburg and Easton sit close together across the river: confirm the land lies in New Jersey and in Warren County before the deed is sent anywhere.

sections.h2: How can you search Warren County land records?
sections.html:
Use the clerk's online public land records search. Choose the guest option and run a search by name to see every recorded document linked to that person, or narrow it to a specific instrument. Major subdivision maps are searchable by municipality, and a full-size map print costs $9 a sheet.

The Computer Access service in the clerk's vault lets visitors look up mortgages, deeds, liens, trade names, inheritance tax waivers, building contracts and maps on terminals. Law firms and title agents that record often can open a charge account with the clerk for recording, certified copies and map copies. Those charge accounts are separate from the accounts set up with the website vendor, which exist only to print copies from the site.

sections.h2: How do Warren County housing numbers look in the Census?
sections.html:
Owners dominate, and values sit between the state's urban core and its wealthiest suburbs. The Census Bureau's 2020-2024 figures for the county are below.

  • Owner-occupied housing rate: 75.1%.
  • Median value of an owner-occupied home: $346,500.
  • Median household income: $100,869.
  • Median gross rent: $1,409.
  • Households: 45,391, with 2.40 people per household.
  • Residents 65 or older: 21.6%.

A median home value of $346,500 puts a typical deed in the range where the state's Realty Transfer Fee schedule for consideration up to $350,000 applies, so many local sales fall near that dividing line.

faqs.q: What is the address of the Warren County Clerk's Office?
faqs.a: 413 Second Street, Belvidere, NJ 07823, in the Warren County Courthouse. The main number is 908-475-6211, and the office is open weekdays from 8:00 am to 4:30 pm. Call ahead for an appointment.

faqs.q: How much does it cost to record a deed in Warren County?
faqs.a: The deed charge is $40 for the first page and $10 for each added page, with a $10 tax abstract on some documents. Add the state Realty Transfer Fee, which depends on the stated consideration.

faqs.q: Can a deed be recorded electronically in Warren County?
faqs.a: Yes. The clerk records documents in person, by mail or electronically. For e-filed documents the Data Recording Page is required for deeds only.

faqs.q: What happens if I leave out the Data Recording Page?
faqs.a: Paper documents without it are charged $20 for indexing, against $10 when the page is attached. Electronically recorded deeds also need the page or the same charge applies.

faqs.q: Is there a fee for filing a veteran's discharge in Warren County?
faqs.a: No. The clerk's fee schedule lists the DD-214 filing as no charge, along with a veteran's ID card and a peddler's license.
